tasks.title: Launch a container
tasks.instructions:
Launch an Ubuntu 24.04 container named `web`:

```bash
lxc launch ubuntu:24.04 web
```

Verify it's running:

```bash
lxc list
```
hints: If the image isn't cached yet, the first launch will download it — be patient.
tasks.solution:
```bash
lxc launch ubuntu:24.04 web
lxc list
```

tasks.title: Set resource limits
tasks.instructions:
Configure the `web` container with resource limits:

```bash
lxc config set web limits.cpu=1 limits.memory=256MiB
```

Verify the limits were set:

```bash
lxc config get web limits.cpu
lxc config get web limits.memory
```
hints: You can set multiple config values in a single lxc config set command.
lxc config get <name> <key> retrieves a single value.
tasks.solution:
```bash
lxc config set web limits.cpu=1 limits.memory=256MiB
lxc config get web limits.cpu
lxc config get web limits.memory
```

tasks.title: Shell into the container
tasks.instructions:
Open an interactive shell inside the `web` container and verify the resource limits are in effect:

```bash
lxc shell web
```

Inside the container, run:
```bash
free -m
nproc
```

You should see 256 MiB of memory and 1 CPU. Type `exit` to leave the shell.
hints: The memory shown by free -m should be approximately 256 MiB.
tasks.solution:
```bash
lxc shell web
# Inside:
free -m
nproc
exit
```

tasks.title: Create a snapshot
tasks.instructions:
Create a snapshot of the `web` container named `clean`:

```bash
lxc snapshot web clean
```

Verify the snapshot exists:

```bash
lxc info web
```

Look for the `Snapshots:` section at the bottom of the output.
hints: lxc info <name> shows snapshot details at the bottom of the output.
You can also check lxc list web — the SNAPSHOTS column will show 1.
tasks.solution:
```bash
lxc snapshot web clean
lxc info web
```

tasks.title: Break and restore
tasks.instructions:
Let's test the snapshot by breaking something and restoring:

1. Remove bash from the container:
```bash
lxc exec web -- rm /usr/bin/bash
```

2. Confirm bash is gone (this should fail):
```bash
lxc exec web -- bash
```

3. Restore from the snapshot:
```bash
lxc restore web clean
```

4. Verify bash works again:
```bash
lxc exec web -- bash -c 'echo restored'
```
hints: After removing bash, lxc exec web -- bash will return an error — that's expected.
lxc restore web clean reverts the container to its state when the snapshot was taken.
tasks.solution:
```bash
lxc exec web -- rm /usr/bin/bash
lxc exec web -- bash  # fails
lxc restore web clean
lxc exec web -- bash -c 'echo restored'
```
